a) World Tamil Diaspora Day

January 12th is celebrated annually as World

Tamil Diaspora Day. This event serves to unite

and encourage Tamils living in various countries,

acknowledging their contributions. Furthermore,

the event aims to pass on our nation's heritage,

art, literature, and culture to the next generation.

Additionally, the fifth edition of "World Tamil

Diaspora Day 2026" was held over two days—

January 11 and 12, 2026—at the Chennai Trade

Centre in Nandambakkam, under the theme

"தமிழால் இைணேவாம் தரணியில் உயர்ேவாம்” (Let us

unite through Tamil and rise globally)." More than

1,552 individuals representing 207 Tamil

associations from 58 countries and 17 Indian

States participated in this event.

For the second time, the 'Tamil Maamani'

award, accompanied by a cash prize of Rs.10

Lakh, was presented to individuals making

15

significant contributions to the growth of Tamil in

foreign countries. Additionally, for the third

consecutive year, the "Kaniyan Poongunranar

Award" was conferred upon eight overseas Tamils

who excelled in seven categories: Science and

Technology, Medicine, Education, Social

Development, Women, Business and Cultural

to children residing in abroad and other Indian

the three-level curriculum offered by the

Tamil Virtual Academy.

Tamil Nadu's tradition of local self-

governance dates to inscriptions at the Sri

Vaikundavasa Perumal Temple, Uthiramerur

(c. 920 A.D., under Parantaka Chola), which

record a written constitution for village

assemblies with election procedures and

eligibility norms. Under the "Kuda Olai

Murai," voters wrote candidates' names on

palm leaves and dropped them into a mud

pot serving as a ballot box—a remarkable

democracy within a monarchy and a

precursor to modern elections. This system

declined under colonial rule.

29

Local governance later evolved through

the Acts of 1854, 1871 and 1884 (creating

District Boards, Taluk Boards and Village

Panchayats), the 1920 Acts, and the Madras

Village Panchayats Act, 1950. The Madras

Panchayats Act, 1958 established a two-tier

system of Village Panchayats and Panchayat

Unions.

The 73rd Constitutional Amendment

(1993) gave Panchayats constitutional

status, and the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Act,

1994 created a three-tier system with

directly elected members, reservations for

SCs/STs and women (50% since 2016), a

State Election Commission, State Finance

Commissions and District Planning

Committees. Functions related to all 29

Eleventh Schedule subjects have been

devolved, making Panchayats vital active

agents for grassroots development.

Each tier performs distinct yet

complementary functions within the

framework of rural governance, while the

devolution of financial resources follows the

principle of subsidiarity, ensuring that the

largest share of funds is allocated to Village

Panchayats, where essential public services

are delivered directly to citizens.

This corridor is a part of Jawalgiri Reserved Forest, starts and ends in Jawalagiri Reserved Forest of Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary by connecting two large habitats i.e. Jawalagiri Reserved Forest (Jawalagiri Range) in Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary, Tamil Nadu and _ Bilikkal State Forest in Bannerghatta National Park, Karnataka State. This route will enable the Trans-Cauvery migration of Elephants and other large mammals between the States of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. There is No bottleneck located in this corridor. heritage, Tamil Nadu is one of the leading States

in India's tourism industry.

2. History of Tourism

Tourism is not a modern invention. Its

roots stretch back to antiquity. In ancient times,

the Greeks and Romans travelled to religious

sites, festivals and the Olympic Games. Wealthy

Romans vacationed at coastal resorts.

Commercial aviation after World War II

transformed tourism from a privilege of the few

into a global mass industry.

3. Key Components of Tourism

Tourism is powered by a complex

ecosystem of interconnected sectors that

seamlessly work together to shape the traveller

2

experience. Facilitating these journeys is the

travel trade, comprising tour operators, travel

agents and online travel aggregators that

package and distribute services. Meanwhile,

destination management structures the entire

experience through tourism boards and

Government bodies, while modern technology

and Destination Management Organisations

(DMOs) optimize operations and planning via

advanced booking platforms and intuitive Travel

Apps.

4. Economic Significance of Tourism

Tourism is a cornerstone of the global

economy. It is one of the top three export

categories for most countries in the world which

directly and indirectly supports hundreds of

millions of jobs globally. In many developing

nations, tourism accounts for a significant share

of GDP and foreign exchange earnings. Tourism

stimulates investment in infrastructures of

3

airports, roads, hotels that benefits entire

communities.

5. Social & Cultural Impact of Tourism

Tourism creates meaningful bridges

between people and civilizations. It fosters cross

cultural understanding and tolerance by

exposing travellers to different lifestyles,

languages and worldviews. It preserves cultural

heritage, protect historical sites, traditional arts

and indigenous practices. While the

commercialization of cultural tourism carries the

risk of commodification, it equally creates

opportunities for sustainable exchange, where

genuine traditions are celebrated and

economically supported by the global audience.

6. Tourism in the Modern Era

The 21st century has reshaped tourism in

profound ways, starting with a remarkable

post-COVID recovery after the pandemic caused

4

the most severe disruption in tourism history

with international arrivals since rebounding

strongly. This era has also witnessed the rise of

the experience economy, as modern travellers

increasingly seek authentic, immersive

experiences over passive sightseeing. On the

technological front, artificial intelligence is

transforming trip planning, personalization,

40. Fairs Division

Through its dedicated Fair Division, the

Tamil Nadu Tourism Development Corporation

actively hosts festivals and fairs to preserve and

promote the region's rich cultural heritage.

40.1 Island Grounds, Chennai

The Tamil Nadu Tourism Development

Corporation (TTDC) is transforming the 21-acre

Island Grounds into a versatile, year-round

event hub. The venue hosted more than

15 small-scale events in 2024-2025, including

community marathons and music concerts. The

Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority

(CMDA) has initiated a new development project

84

along the eastern side of the grounds to support

this growing calendar of public activities.

40.2 50th India Tourist and Industrial Fair,

2026

Since 1974, Tamil Nadu Tourism

Development Corporation has hosted the annual

India Tourist and Industrial Fair from January to

March each year, running for 70 days at Island

Grounds, Chennai. In 2025-2026 the 50th edition

of the fair was held at the same venue. The fair

featured food stalls and entertainment to draw

tourists, families and children and showcased

pavilions from 43 government departments,

including the Tamil Nadu Tourism Department.

41. Conclusion

Tourism is far more than holidays and

sightseeing. It is a powerful force that shapes

economies, bridges cultures, transforms

85

landscapes and enriches human experience.

When managed thoughtfully and sustainably, it

can be one of humanity's most potent tools for

global understanding, economic development

and the celebration of the world's extraordinary

diversity. As the world grows more

interconnected, tourism will remain one of the

defining activities of the human story.

Tamil Nadu with its unmatched heritage,

improving infrastructure, has all the ingredients

to become not just India's top tourism

destination but a global benchmark for

responsible tourism.
